title: Eukaryotic Gene Regulation Layers
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Biology
description: Interactive MicroSim for exploring chromatin, transcriptional, post-transcriptional, translational, and post-translational regulation layers.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to organize the five major layers of eukaryotic gene regulation and explain how activation and repression cues act at each checkpoint.
prerequisites: Can describe the central dogma of molecular biology

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive exploration with progressive disclosure and flow-based storytelling
keyQuestions: What molecular events either open or close chromatin at the start of gene regulation?
How do promoter/enhancer interactions change transcription outcomes?
Where can cells intercept a message after transcription but before translation finishes?
commonMisconceptions: Only transcription regulates genes; later checkpoints do not matter.
Activation and repression always happen at separate loci instead of within the same layer.
assessmentOpportunities: Student explains one activation and one repression strategy for each layer.
Learner narrates the flow animation and predicts what happens if a checkpoint fails.
